verdict.rationale: Osborne Clarke publishes pricing pages that state hourly rate ranges (£190–£870 for immigration, £240–£870 for employment tribunal work, excluding VAT) and indicative matter-level fee bands (e.g. naturalisation £4,000–£5,000; tribunal claims £25,000–£35,000 and £35,000–£55,000 by complexity). That meets the story's bar of not leaving cost entirely opaque. The disclosure covers only two individual-facing practice areas, though, and none of the core commercial service pages (corporate/EC&VC, IP, data, financing) show any pricing. Missing for 10: pricing or billing-practice disclosure for commercial practice areas, published alternative fee arrangements (fixed-fee or capped models), firm-wide billing policies, independent corroboration.
